definitions.explanation: The formal ceremony held for a deceased person. In Japan, funerals typically follow Buddhist traditions, though Shinto and Christian services also occur.

examples.japanese: {葬儀|そうぎ}は{明日|あした}{行|おこな}われる。
examples.english: The funeral will be held tomorrow.

examples.japanese: {葬儀|そうぎ}に{参列|さんれつ}するために{黒|くろ}い{服|ふく}を{着|き}た。
examples.english: I wore black clothes to attend the funeral.

examples.japanese: {葬儀|そうぎ}の{準備|じゅんび}は{葬儀社|そうぎしゃ}に{任|まか}せることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Funeral preparations are often left to the funeral home.

notes:
USAGE:
The standard formal word for a funeral ceremony. In Japan, funerals often consist of two parts: {通夜|つや} (wake, held the evening before) and {葬儀|そうぎ}/{告別式|こくべつしき} (funeral/farewell ceremony).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {葬儀|そうぎ}を{行|おこな}う (to hold a funeral)
- {葬儀|そうぎ}に{参列|さんれつ}する (to attend a funeral)
- {葬儀社|そうぎしゃ} (funeral home, funeral director)
- {葬儀場|そうぎじょう} (funeral hall)
- {家族葬|かぞくそう} (family-only funeral)
